questions.title: Time complexity of binary search
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each step, so it runs in O(log n).

questions.title: Which data structure is best for LRU cache?
questions.explanation: An LRU cache needs O(1) get/put. HashMap plus a doubly linked list supports both.

questions.title: HTTP 429 typically means
questions.explanation: 429 Too Many Requests is returned when rate limits are exceeded.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.statement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Assume exactly one solution exists. This is a common LinkedIn screening question.
questions.constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4. You may not use the same element twice.
hints: Use a hashmap from value -> index.
For each number x, look up target - x.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.statement: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid. Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
hints: Push opening brackets and pop on matching close.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hints: Sliding window + set/map of last seen index.

questions.title: Merge K Sorted Lists
questions.statement: You are given an array of k linked-lists, each sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it.

questions.title: How would you design a URL shortener like those used at LinkedIn?
questions.prompt: Walk through requirements, API, data model, hashing/encoding, scale (reads vs writes), and how you handle collisions and analytics.
keyPoints: Base62 encoding of a unique id
Cache hot URLs, shard by key
questions.modelAnswer: Start with create/redirect APIs and a mapping of shortCode -> longUrl. Generate unique IDs (Snowflake or DB sequence) and encode in Base62. Put a cache in front of the DB for hot keys, replicate for read-heavy traffic, and store analytics asynchronously. Handle collisions by retrying with a new id.

questions.title: Explain REST vs GraphQL
questions.prompt: When would you pick REST, and when GraphQL, in a large product company?
questions.modelAnswer: REST fits public APIs, HTTP caching, and simple CRUD. GraphQL fits complex client views that need nested data without multiple round trips. At scale you still version carefully, add persisted queries, and protect the graph with depth/cost limits.

questions.title: CAP theorem in interviews
questions.prompt: Explain CAP and give a real example of CP vs AP systems.
keyPoints: Network partitions force a consistency vs availability choice
AP example: Dynamo-style stores with eventual consistency
questions.modelAnswer: During a partition you cannot have both linearizable consistency and full availability. CP systems refuse some requests to stay consistent. AP systems keep serving and reconcile later. Most product systems mix both: strong consistency for payments, eventual for feeds.
